newsitem.title: USA: Most U.S. debt futures open slightly lower.
newsitem.headline: Most U.S. debt futures open slightly lower.

text.p: Most U.S. debt futures opened slightly lower, but action was quiet as players bided their time before key data later this week.

"It's typical quiet Monday action," said John Kadich, a floor analyst with Dean Witter. He said players may lighten up positions heading into important numbers later this week, but said he expects it to remain quiet Monday. He pegged intraday support at 109-27/32 to 109-28/32 and resistance at 110-14/32.
The data line-up begins Tuesday with April retail sales. April producer and consumer price data will be released later in the week.

Floor traders said a weak dollar overnight lent a bearish beginning tone to debt futures. Some said a seller of up to 1,500 June contracts hit the June bond pit early, also helping set the dim opening tone.
But overall they said the mood was noncommittal heading into the flood of key data this week.

One broker said expectations were for April retail sales on Tuesday to be friendly for the market. A Reuters poll of economists showed an average forecast for an 0.3 percent drop in retail sales overall, with an 0.1-percent gain excluding autos.
In the previous report, overall sales rose 0.1 percent and sales ex-autos gained 0.5 percent.
Don Pullen, bond trading floor manager for ED and F Man, said traders were preparing for a week of mostly flat data.
"That would be friendly for the market," Pullen said.
If that is the case, then this week's economic news will not change the perception there is a 50/50 chance of a Federal Reserve rate hike May 20, he said.
He pegged near-term support at 109-27/32, the overnight June T-bond low, and resistance at 110-16/32. The 6-7/8 percent yield equivalent is roughly 110-15/32, traders said.

At 0835 CDT/1335 GMT, June T-bonds fell 1/32 to 110-6/32, 10-year notes were down 1/32 at 107-12/32, munibonds were 1/32 higher at 115-26/32, September T-bills were up 0.015 at 94.535, and December Eurodollars were flat at 93.72. ((Derivatives desk 312-408-8750))
